exhibit.title: First LAN test record
exhibit.text:
PC-A: 192.168.10.10, mask 255.255.255.0
PC-B: 192.168.10.20, mask 255.255.255.0
Both PCs connect to the same switch.
PC-A ping to 192.168.10.20: replies received

prompt: What does the successful test establish?
options: PC-A received ICMP replies from PC-B during this test.
PC-A can reach Internet destinations through the switch.
Every application on PC-B is available to PC-A.
The switch has saved the PCs’ addresses in startup configuration.
explanation: The result establishes the tested ICMP exchange between the two local addresses at that time. Other destinations, applications and saved configuration require their own checks.

whyWrong.1: No Internet destination or router path was tested.
whyWrong.2: A ping tests ICMP, not every service on the destination.
whyWrong.3: PC addressing is endpoint configuration; a ping does not verify any device’s saved configuration.

exhibit.title: Context help
exhibit.text:
S1# show ip interface brief ?
  |     Output modifiers
  <cr>

prompt: What does `<cr>` in this context-help response mean?
options: The command just completed successfully.
Another required argument must follow.
Enter can complete the command here.
Enter will display another page of output.
explanation: The `<cr>` marker represents a carriage return. It indicates that the command can be completed by pressing Enter; other listed choices may be optional continuations.

whyWrong.0: Context help lists valid choices; it has not executed the command.
whyWrong.1: The completion marker means a required argument is not missing at this point.
whyWrong.3: This is command help, not the --More-- output pager.

prompt: Which command saves the active configuration to the normal startup configuration?
options: copy startup-config running-config
copy running-config startup-config
show startup-config
show running-config
explanation: The copy command names the source first and destination second. Copy running configuration to startup configuration, accept the intended destination, and verify the saved setting.

whyWrong.0: The source and destination are reversed; this does not save the active configuration.
whyWrong.2: This displays the saved configuration rather than updating it.
whyWrong.3: This displays the active configuration rather than saving it.

prompt: On the classic IOS lab device, which two statements describe running and startup configuration? Choose two.
options: Running configuration contains only changes since the last save.
Running configuration represents the currently active settings.
Startup configuration changes whenever you enter end.
Startup configuration supplies saved settings for a normal boot.
Displaying startup configuration copies it into running configuration.
explanation: The active configuration and the saved startup configuration serve different purposes. Leaving configuration mode or displaying a configuration does not copy it. The Packet Tracer project is another separate item.

whyWrong.0: Running configuration represents the active configuration, not just the unsaved difference.
whyWrong.2: end changes command mode; saving requires a separate action.
whyWrong.4: A show command displays the saved settings without applying them.

prompt: Both PCs share one switch LAN. Which correction matches the supplied plan?
options: Keep both addresses because their subnet masks match.
Enter PC-A’s address as PC-B’s default gateway.
Change PC-B’s address to 192.168.10.20.
Rename PC-B’s workspace label without changing its address.
explanation: PC-B repeats PC-A’s address instead of using its own assigned value. These separate hosts need distinct addresses on this LAN. Correct PC-B to the supplied value before interpreting a communication test.

whyWrong.0: Matching masks do not make a duplicate host address correct.
whyWrong.1: A gateway setting would not remove the duplicate address, and this local test needs no gateway.
whyWrong.3: A workspace name does not change the address configured on the endpoint.

exhibit.title: Representative CLI excerpt
exhibit.text:
Switch> show running-config
             ^
% Invalid input detected at '^' marker.

prompt: Why is this command rejected on a default lab switch?
options: The display command belongs in global configuration.
The displayed command needs an interface selected first.
The command requires privileged EXEC on this device.
The hostname argument must follow running-config.
explanation: The > prompt indicates user EXEC. Enter enable to reach privileged EXEC, then run show running-config. Check the prompt before treating a parser error as a spelling problem.

whyWrong.0: Global configuration changes settings; this display is a privileged EXEC command on the lab switch.
whyWrong.1: The whole running configuration is not selected through an interface context.
whyWrong.3: The hostname is a setting inside the configuration, not an argument to this show command.

exhibit.title: Separate device and project checks
exhibit.text:
Workspace label: S1
Saved project filename: 00-first-lan.pkt
Current CLI prompt: S1#

prompt: You need evidence that hostname S1 is in the switch’s startup configuration. Which additional check directly supplies it?
options: Find S1 in the workspace device label.
Find S1 in show running-config.
Close and reopen the CLI tab to read its prompt.
Find hostname S1 in show startup-config.
explanation: Inspect startup configuration to verify the saved device setting. The prompt verifies the active name, while the file and workspace names describe the simulator project.

whyWrong.0: The workspace label is separate from the IOS configuration.
whyWrong.1: Running configuration shows the active name, which may still be unsaved.
whyWrong.2: Reopening the tab shows the currently active name, not whether it was saved.
